skill.name: firecrawl-web
skill.description: Use Firecrawl to fetch web pages, capture screenshots, extract structured data, search the web, and crawl documentation sites from Claude Code, Codex, or Claude.
skill.summary: Use Firecrawl for web scraping, screenshots, search, extraction, and documentation crawling.
skill.author: BexTuychiev

security_audit.summary: Confirmed risks include external Firecrawl requests for arbitrary URLs, screenshot generation, local file writes, and loading .env files including ~/.env. Most SKILL.md and README.md detections are false positives because they are markdown examples or normal skill path references; no prompt injection text was found.

remediation.suggestion: Load only the FIRECRAWL_API_KEY value from the active environment or a dedicated skill config file, and remove Path.home() / ".env" loading.

remediation.issue: Third-party exposure of URLs and page content
remediation.suggestion: Warn users before sending private or internal URLs to Firecrawl, and document that screenshots, prompts, and crawl targets leave the local machine.
Restrict screenshot and crawl outputs to an explicit workspace directory, validate paths, and avoid silent overwrites.
Recommend a scoped environment variable or dedicated permissions-controlled file instead of appending secrets to a global home .env file.

static_findings.snippet: # Load .env from current directory and home directory
- **Screenshots** - Capture full-page screenshots of any URL
Each page costs one credit. Set a reasonable limit to avoid burning through your quota.

finding_verdicts.reason: urllib.request is imported for later screenshot URL retrieval from Firecrawl. The import is not dangerous alone, but it is part of real external network behavior.
The code downloads a screenshot URL returned by Firecrawl to a caller-selected output path. This is intended behavior, but it is a real external network transfer.
The screenshot command writes decoded image bytes to the caller-provided output path. This can overwrite or create arbitrary files allowed by the local process.
The crawl command writes markdown files under a caller-provided output directory. The filenames are generated, but the destination directory is user controlled.
The dotenv import is used by main() to load environment files for the Firecrawl API key. This confirms environment-based secret handling in the skill.
load_dotenv() loads variables from a local .env file into the process. This is normal credential loading, but it can expose secrets to the running script.
The script explicitly loads ~/.env from the user home directory. A home-wide .env can contain unrelated secrets that should not be loaded by this tool.
The python-dotenv loader is imported and then used to read .env files. It supports real environment secret access in this skill.
The loader reads variables from a local .env file at runtime. This is common API key handling, but it is still environment file access.
The loader reads ~/.env from the user home directory. That broadens the script environment beyond the one Firecrawl key it needs.
The base64 decode converts Firecrawl image data into screenshot bytes before writing a PNG. It is not used to hide code, commands, or payloads.
The comment documents intentional loading of both current-directory and home-directory .env files. This confirms the sensitive-file access is deliberate.
The code reads ~/.env directly, which may contain secrets unrelated to Firecrawl. Loading a global home environment file is a real sensitive data exposure risk.

content.value_statement: AI coding tools often need current web pages, screenshots, or documentation that is outside the local workspace. This skill uses Firecrawl to fetch, search, extract, and crawl web content through clear commands.
actual_capabilities: Fetches a URL as clean markdown, with an option to keep only main content.
Captures full-page website screenshots and can save them as PNG files.
Extracts structured fields from a page using a user-provided schema and optional prompt.
Runs Firecrawl web searches with a configurable result limit.
Crawls documentation sites and can save crawled pages into a local directory.
limitations: Requires a Firecrawl API key and installed Python dependencies.
Sends requested URLs, search terms, and extraction prompts to Firecrawl.
Consumes Firecrawl credits for scraping, screenshots, search, extraction, and crawling.
Does not provide custom browser cookies or authenticated session handling in the bundled script.

use_cases.title: Review External Documentation
use_cases.description: Fetch or crawl framework documentation so an assistant can answer implementation questions with current source material.

use_cases.title: Extract Page Details
use_cases.description: Pull product titles, prices, features, or similar fields from public pages using a defined extraction schema.

use_cases.title: Capture Web Evidence
use_cases.description: Save page screenshots and markdown snapshots for research notes, issue reports, or content review workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Fetch Page Markdown
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for readable page content.
prompt_templates.prompt: Get the markdown from this URL and summarize the main points: https://example.com

prompt_templates.title: Search Current Information
prompt_templates.scenario: Find recent or external web material before answering.
prompt_templates.prompt: Search the web for the latest stable release notes for this framework and return the top three useful sources.

prompt_templates.title: Extract Specific Fields
prompt_templates.scenario: Use a schema to pull structured information from one page.
prompt_templates.prompt: Extract the title, price, feature list, and availability from this product page using a small schema.

prompt_templates.title: Crawl Documentation Site
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow for learning a new library from its docs.
prompt_templates.prompt: Crawl this documentation site with a limit of 30 pages, then identify the installation steps and core API concepts.

output_examples.input: Get the markdown from a public documentation page.
output: A cleaned markdown version of the page content.
Navigation and footer content can be reduced with the main content option.
The assistant can summarize the returned text or cite key sections.

output_examples.input: Take a screenshot of a public landing page.
output_examples.output: The skill saves a full-page PNG screenshot or returns a screenshot link from Firecrawl.

output_examples.input: Crawl a documentation site with a page limit.
output: A bounded set of crawled documentation pages is returned.
When an output directory is provided, each page is saved as a markdown file.

best_practices: Use clear page limits before crawling large sites.
Avoid private, authenticated, or internal URLs unless Firecrawl use is approved.
Store the Firecrawl API key with least exposure and rotate it if it appears in logs.
anti_patterns: Do not crawl broad domains without a limit or clear purpose.
Do not send confidential pages, customer data, or secrets to external scraping services.
Do not save screenshots or crawled pages into shared folders without checking the contents.

faq.question: What service does this skill use?
faq.answer: It uses Firecrawl through the firecrawl Python package and requires a Firecrawl API key.

faq.question: Can it fetch current web pages?
faq.answer: Yes. It can scrape public pages as markdown and search the web through Firecrawl.

faq.question: Can it take screenshots?
faq.answer: Yes. It requests full-page website screenshots through Firecrawl and can save them locally.

faq.question: Does it work with private websites?
faq.answer: The bundled script does not pass browser cookies or authenticated session data.

faq.question: Where does it store output files?
faq.answer: Screenshots are saved to the requested output path, and crawled pages can be saved to a requested directory.

faq.question: What should users avoid sending?
faq.answer: Users should avoid confidential URLs, internal systems, secrets, and pages containing private data.
